name: Medium Pink
lede: Medium Pink is a saturated, slightly bluish pink, a plain descriptive name that a 2010 online color survey put on the map and that no color book treats as a color of its own.

sections.title: A plain description
sections.body:
The library records Medium Pink only from a 2010 crowd-sourced color survey and a Wikipedia list, with no older source [1]. It is a modifier name, "medium" plus [[pink]], and the nearest ISCC-NBS category is deep purplish pink, about 5.6 units away [1]. The nearest named look-alike is [[hot-pink]] [2].

The color books hold nothing on it as a color. The one hit in Paterson's *Dictionary of Colour* is an aside defining coral pink as a deep orange-pink, sometimes a medium pink or a yellowish pink [3]. That is the word *medium* used loosely, not a named color [3]. The survey swatch is also a different color from some other "medium pink" definitions, so the name should not be read as a fixed standard [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole, and bright pinks of this strength are mostly a feature of modern dyes and screens [4].
